newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat after active c.bank support.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat after active c.bank support.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 216.00/70 per dollar, almost unchanged from 215-217 in the morning on the interbank market as the central bank and state-owned banks actively offered dollars, dealers said.
"Active dollar sales by the central bank and three commercial banks locked trade in a narrow range, stabilising the lev near 216," a dealer said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment. Foreign currency was sought mainly for short-covering or meeting pending payments, traders said.
"The dollar-bullish sentiment of the past two days subsided and trade was very quiet," another dealer said.

At the beginning of this week the lev was pushed down to 223 per dollar due to expectations of a sharp dollar rise following news that the IMF has again postponed a second tranche of funding, dealers said.
The lev could weaken on Thursday due to the longer period to value date of that day's spot deals, traders said.

"But if the central bank continues its active dollar sales in cooperation with large state banks I do not expect a sharp lev's fall," a third dealer said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
